repo.name: selinux
repo.description: This is the upstream repository for the Security Enhanced Linux (SELinux) userland libraries and tools. The software provided by this project complements the SELinux features integrated into the Linux kernel and is used by Linux distributions. All bugs and patches should be submitted to selinux@vger.kernel.org

readme.summary: Well-structured installation guide for developers building from source, but lacks user-facing quick start examples and practical usage guidance.
readme.top_issue: No quick start example showing how to actually use libselinux after installation - no code samples, API usage, or common operations demonstrated

injection_risks.description: The function send_request uses user-controlled data (data1 and data2) to construct a message for sending over a socket. Although the lengths of these strings are checked, there is still a risk of buffer overflow or information disclosure if an attacker can manipulate the contents of these strings.

The function receive_response uses user-controlled data (outdata) to store received response. There is a risk of buffer overflow or information disclosure if an attacker can manipulate the contents of this string.

critical_findings: Potential buffer overflow or information disclosure in send_request and receive_response functions
Lack of input validation for function parameters
security.summary: The code has some security concerns, including potential injection risks and lack of input validation, but overall it appears to be well-structured and follows good practices.

common_complaints: SWIG binding issues (incorrect marshalling, missing wrappers)
Memory safety bugs (UAF, SIGBUS from mmap)
Integration problems with systemd and modern systems
Build/compilation failures and installation path inconsistencies
Python import errors and circular dependencies
sentiment.summary: libselinux shows signs of abandonment with 11 open issues (mostly critical bugs), zero maintainer responses, and longstanding architectural problems incompatible with modern Linux systems.

red_flags: Lack of clear instructions for new contributors
communication.summary: Responses are generally helpful and clear, but could be more welcoming to new contributors.

concerns: No commits in past 6 months despite last commit being recent (Feb 2, 2026)
120 open issues with no recent activity suggests backlog accumulation
Zero closed issues in past 6 months indicates no active issue resolution
No merged PRs in past 6 months shows development has stalled
No active contributors in past 6 months
Unknown release date suggests release process may be abandoned
positive_signals: Recent last commit date (Feb 2, 2026) indicates repository is not fully abandoned
maintenance.summary: libselinux appears stale with recent activity but no ongoing maintenance, indicated by zero commits, issues, and PRs in the past 6 months combined with 120 unresolved open issues.

governance.summary: The project has documented decision-making processes and multiple maintainers, but lacks a succession plan or contributor ladder.
